newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Vodafone sees Australia mobile growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Vodafone sees Australia mobile growth.

text.p: Mobile phone group Vodafone Australia, a unit of Britian's Vodafone Plc, said on Wednesday it expected up to 5.5 million mobile digital phones to be sold in Australia over the next three years.
Vodafone Australia managing director John Rohan told a telecommunications conference that the replacement of analogue mobiles would stimulate the growth of digital mobiles.

"Up to five and a half milllion mobile phones will be sold in Australia in the next three years as the markets grows and older analogue mobiles are upgraded to digital, spurring further rapid growth of the mobile communications market," Rohan said.
Australia with a population of about 18 million people has one of the world's highest pentration rates of mobile phones.
The country has about four million mobile phone owners.
Rohan said forecasts indicated that Australia's mobile market would grow to six to seven million by 2000, an increase of around three million mobile phones from the current four million in use.
"In addition, however, the phase-out of analogue technology is underway. This will involve the upgrading of over 2.5 million analogue mobile phones to digital over the next three years," Rohan said.
